raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Before submitting

- [x] I agree to license this contribution under the terms of [LICENSE.txt](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/LICENSE.txt).
- [x] I ran `pre-commit run` and committed any formatting changes.
- [x] I reviewed the Hard Rules in the `AGENTS.md` for each directory this PR touches (see [root AGENTS.md § Reviewing a PR](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/AGENTS.md#reviewing-a-pr-human-or-agent)) and my changes comply, or I explain the exception below.
- [x] I added GitHub labels: one `cat-*`, one or more `area:*` / `op:*`, and one `orig-*` (see [label list](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/labels)).

## Affected area

FE OSS kernels or CuTeDSL

- `python/cudnn/gemm/frost/epilogue_codegen.py` (shared FROST GEMM epilogue emitter)
- `test/python/gemm/frost/test_epilogue_cmp_ops.py` (new)

## Summary

- Under fp32 compute, `_emit_binary_ext` now emits each `cmp_*` epilogue op as a native vector compare selected to 1/0:
  `cutlass._mlir_helpers.vector.where(a OP b, full_like(a, 1.0), full_like(a, 0.0))`, with OP one of `==`, `!=`, `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`
  (the new module constant `_CMP_PY_OPS`, next to `_CMP_OPS`).
  These lower to `arith.cmpf` with the IEEE predicates OEQ, UNE, OLT, OLE, OGT and OGE. Before, every `cmp_*` op was emulated as
  `step01(d) = min(max(floor(d) + 1, 0), 1)` over `d = a - b` or `b - a`.
- INT32 compute keeps the existing step form (see "API and compatibility impact"); `_step01` is unchanged and still serves the
  logical ops, `mod` and the backward ops.
- New SM120 regression test `test_cmp_ops_follow_ieee_for_nonfinite_operands_sm120`: the six ops with the aux on either side of the
  compare, plus the isnan and isfinite idioms.

## Why

The emulated compares are exact only for finite operands. `a - b` is NaN when either operand is NaN, and when `a` and `b` are the
same infinity. `cute.math.max` / `cute.math.min` default to `propagate_nan=False` and lower to the NaN-ignoring
`arith.maxnumf` / `arith.minnumf` (PTX `max.f32` / `min.f32` without `.NaN`), so `step01(NaN)` is 0. As a result:

- a NaN operand made `cmp_lt` and `cmp_gt` return 1 (IEEE: 0); `cmp_eq`, `cmp_neq`, `cmp_le` and `cmp_ge` happened to be right;
- equal same-signed infinities inverted all six ops: `cmp_eq`, `cmp_le` and `cmp_ge` returned 0, `cmp_neq`, `cmp_lt` and `cmp_gt` returned 1;
- so the isnan idiom `cmp_neq(C, C)` reported +-inf as NaN, and the isfinite idiom `cmp_lt(abs(C), inf)` returned 1 for inf and NaN.

Minimal reproducer (the new test): dense `sm120_matmul` through `jit_from_cudnn_graph` with
`CONFIG_sm120_128x128x128_16x16x32_cluster1x1_warps4x2`, bf16 A/B, M = N = K = 128, fp32 intermediate and compute, fp32 outputs
`y = cmp_op(C, X)` and `y = cmp_op(X, C)` with `X` an fp32 per-element aux. Rows of C are forced to +inf, -inf or NaN by putting that
value in `A[:, 0]` with `B[0, :] = 1`. On develop 24a8cd43, in both operand orders, every equal-infinity cell is wrong for all six ops
(1024 per 16-row band), every NaN cell is wrong for `cmp_lt` / `cmp_gt` (2048 per band, NaN on either side), and every finite cell is
right (equal values, +-0.5 / +-1 offsets, finite vs +-inf, 0 vs +-subnormal). The plain MoE templates and the dense block-scale
template show the same pattern (ad hoc checks below).

Through the public `graph.execute()` path on the same GPU (with `CUDNN_FRONTEND_ENABLE_FROST_ENGINES=1`, since the FROST GEMM engine
is opt-in), the first cuDNN backend plan (engine 10) for `y = cmp_op(C, X)` returns IEEE masks, and the FROST plan (engine 20400) did
not on develop. So the two engines gave the same graph different results,
while Rule 9 of `python/cudnn/AGENTS.md` asks backend and FROST to keep the same semantics for a graph both support. With this
change they agree (counts under Testing).

A native compare has IEEE semantics by construction: the ordered predicates are false when an operand is NaN, the unordered `UNE` is
true, and equal infinities compare equal. No arithmetic on `a - b` can give `cmp_eq` / `cmp_le` / `cmp_ge` for equal infinities, so
patching the NaN handling of `max` / `min` would not be enough. `vector.where` over a vector compare is the lowering `binary_select`
and the mainloop K-tail mask already use in this module, so this adds no new CuTe DSL dependency.

The change is outside `python/cudnn/gemm/frost/sm120/` because, since #1993, the emitter lives only in the shared
`python/cudnn/gemm/frost/epilogue_codegen.py`, whose `_emit_pointwise_dag` both arch families call
(`sm120/epilogue_codegen.py:827`, `sm100/epilogue_codegen.py:498`). There is no per-family copy to fix instead.

Found in an audit of the SM120 Frost kernel templates (finding B09).

## Related issues

None.

Related PRs from the same audit that change `python/cudnn/gemm/frost/epilogue_codegen.py`:

- #2022 (G4.4, int32-compute epilogue ops) makes SM120 decline int32-compute `cmp_*` ops (in `sm120/compiler.py`). Those are the only
  graphs that still reach the step form left in the `cmp_*` branch of `_emit_binary_ext`; SM100 has no such check (see "API and
  compatibility impact").
- #2030 (G4.1, `mod`), #2026 (G4.3, default `relu_backward`) and #2009 (B10, `relu` / `relu_backward` with a slope) change other
  branches of `_emit_binary_ext`; G4.1 and G4.3 also replace step forms there.
- #2012 (G4.2), #2025 (B11), #2014 (B13) and #2013 (B14) change other emitters in the same file.

`git merge-tree` merges each of these branches with this one without conflicts.

## API and compatibility impact

- No API change.
- Numerics: under fp32 compute, `cmp_*` masks change only where an operand is NaN or both operands are the same infinity; they now
  match IEEE comparison and torch, and in the `graph.execute()` check under Testing they match cuDNN backend engine 10 on the same
  graphs. Masks for finite operands are unchanged.
- SM100: the emitter is shared, so the SM100 tree (dense, block-scale, MoE, the split-K reduction epilogue and SM100 mainloop-fusion
  transforms) gets the same fix. It was not run on SM100 hardware here; the existing SM100 cmp cases in
  `test_matmul_epilogue_fusion.py::test_pointwise_mode_coverage` (finite inputs) exercise the new code on SM100 CI.
- INT32 compute is unchanged: a `cmp_*` node with `compute_data_type=INT32` still takes the step form and still fails at build with
  `TypeError: floor is only supported for floating-point types`. That failure is a separate audit finding (G4.4); its PR #2022
  declines such graphs on SM120. `sm100/compiler.py` has no such check, so removing the int32 step form is left for a follow-up.
- Chains with `cmp_*` ops render different kernel source, so their cached kernels are rebuilt once.

## Testing

GPU: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (SM120), CUDA 13.4, nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.7.1, torch 2.14.0+cu130, cuDNN 9.24,
frontend bindings built from develop 24a8cd43. All commands from `test/python`.

Regression test, RED on develop (a detached worktree of 24a8cd43 with only the new test copied in) and GREEN on this branch:

```
python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider -p no:xdist gemm/frost/test_epilogue_cmp_ops.py
# develop 24a8cd43: 1 failed, 1 warning in 1.89s
#   cmp_eq/neq/lt/le/gt/ge @ C=+inf, X=+inf: 1024 cells each; @ C=-inf, X=-inf: 1024 each
#   cmp_lt/gt @ C=NaN, X=0: 2048 each; @ C finite, X=NaN: 2048 each
#   the same cells for each cmp_op(X, C) output (aux on the left)
#   isnan @ C=+-inf: 2048 each; isfinite @ C=+-inf and C=NaN: 2048 each
# this branch:      1 passed, 1 warning in 1.80s
```

The test is collected by `-k frost`, `-k sm120` and the default `-m L0` sweep.

Related existing tests:

```
python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider -p no:xdist gemm/frost -k sm120
# develop 24a8cd43: 1 failed, 1036 passed, 82 skipped, 9789 deselected, 201 warnings in 292.75s
# this branch:      1 failed, 1037 passed, 82 skipped, 9789 deselected in 13.16s
#   (warm kernel cache; files of the branch head)
```

The extra pass is the new test. The one failure, `test_matmul.py::test_sm120_epi_vec_clamp_and_stg_only`, fails the same way on
develop (`_use_tma_store_epi(chain, cfg100)` is False for the SM100 config on an SM120 GPU) and does not involve `cmp_*` ops.

Host-side analyzer and codegen tests. None of them builds a `cmp_*` graph (the mainloop file names the `cmp_*` ops only in its
`ZERO_PRESERVING_OPS` registry check, which renders nothing), so they show only that the rendering of other ops through `_emit_op`
is unchanged. Their SM100 GPU cases skip on SM120:

```
python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider -p no:xdist gemm/frost/test_multi_gemm.py gemm/frost/test_matmul_mainloop_fusion.py
# develop 24a8cd43: 22 passed, 199 skipped
# this branch:      22 passed, 199 skipped
```

Ad hoc checks (scripts not committed):

- Public `graph.execute()` path with `CUDNN_FRONTEND_ENABLE_FROST_ENGINES=1`, one graph `y = cmp_op(C, X)` per op (bf16 A/B,
  M = N = K = 128, fp32 aux `X`, the regression test's +-inf / NaN rows), each plan's mask compared with torch: the FROST plan (engine
  20400) gets 2048 wrong cells for `cmp_eq`, `cmp_neq`, `cmp_le` and `cmp_ge` and 6144 for `cmp_lt` and `cmp_gt` on develop, and 0
  for all six on this branch. The cuDNN backend plan (engine 10) gets 0 for all six on both.
- Dense block-scale template `sm120_block_scale_matmul` (MXFP8: e4m3 A/B with e8m0 block scales, block 32, M = N = 256, K = 512):
  12 masks, `cmp_op(C + S, X)` and `cmp_op(X, C + S)` for the six ops, with fp32 aux `S` and `X` holding +-inf / NaN rows and one mask
  stored as bf16: develop 163840 wrong cells, this branch 0.
- Dense `sm120_matmul` (M = N = 256, K = 128): the same 12 masks plus a per-row aux (`cmp_ge(C + S, r)`) and a per-column aux on the
  left (`cmp_lt(q, C + S)`); every compare is fed by the prior `add`, not by C directly: develop 176384 wrong cells, this branch 0.
- Plain MoE templates `sm120_moe_grouped_matmul_fwd` and `sm120_moe_grouped_matmul_fwd_swap_ab` (E = 2, S = 256, N = K = 128), six
  `cmp_*` masks of the MoE output against an fp32 aux with +-inf / NaN: develop 53248 wrong cells in total, this branch 0.
- `cmp_*` with `compute_data_type=INT32` on the dense template: develop and this branch both fail at build with the same `floor`
  TypeError (unchanged, see above).

Not tested: SM100-family hardware (none available here); the MoE block-scale templates `sm120_moe_grouped_block_scale_matmul_fwd`
and `sm120_moe_grouped_block_scale_matmul_fwd_swap_ab` with `cmp_*` ops (same emitter and aux-load code).

  `cutlass._mlir_helpers.vector.where(a OP b, full_like(a, 1.0), full_like(a, 0.0))`, with OP one of `==`, `!=`, `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`
  (the new module constant `_CMP_PY_OPS`, next to `_CMP_OPS`).
  These lower to `arith.cmpf` with the IEEE predicates OEQ, UNE, OLT, OLE, OGT and OGE. Before, every `cmp_*` op was emulated as
  `step01(d) = min(max(floor(d) + 1, 0), 1)` over `d = a - b` or `b - a`.
- INT32 compute keeps the existing step form (see "API and compatibility impact"); `_step01` is unchanged and still serves the
  logical ops, `mod` and the backward ops.
- New SM120 regression test `test_cmp_ops_follow_ieee_for_nonfinite_operands_sm120`: the six ops with the aux on either side of the
  compare, plus the isnan and isfinite idioms.

## Why

The emulated compares are exact only for finite operands. `a - b` is NaN when either operand is NaN, and when `a` and `b` are the
same infinity. `cute.math.max` / `cute.math.min` default to `propagate_nan=False` and lower to the NaN-ignoring
`arith.maxnumf` / `arith.minnumf` (PTX `max.f32` / `min.f32` without `.NaN`), so `step01(NaN)` is 0. As a result:

- a NaN operand made `cmp_lt` and `cmp_gt` return 1 (IEEE: 0); `cmp_eq`, `cmp_neq`, `cmp_le` and `cmp_ge` happened to be right;
- equal same-signed infinities inverted all six ops: `cmp_eq`, `cmp_le` and `cmp_ge` returned 0, `cmp_neq`, `cmp_lt` and `cmp_gt` returned 1;
- so the isnan idiom `cmp_neq(C, C)` reported +-inf as NaN, and the isfinite idiom `cmp_lt(abs(C), inf)` returned 1 for inf and NaN.

Minimal reproducer (the new test): dense `sm120_matmul` through `jit_from_cudnn_graph` with
`CONFIG_sm120_128x128x128_16x16x32_cluster1x1_warps4x2`, bf16 A/B, M = N = K = 128, fp32 intermediate and compute, fp32 outputs
`y = cmp_op(C, X)` and `y = cmp_op(X, C)` with `X` an fp32 per-element aux. Rows of C are forced to +inf, -inf or NaN by putting that
value in `A[:, 0]` with `B[0, :] = 1`. On develop 24a8cd43, in both operand orders, every equal-infinity cell is wrong for all six ops
(1024 per 16-row band), every NaN cell is wrong for `cmp_lt` / `cmp_gt` (2048 per band, NaN on either side), and every finite cell is
right (equal values, +-0.5 / +-1 offsets, finite vs +-inf, 0 vs +-subnormal). The plain MoE templates and the dense block-scale
template show the same pattern (ad hoc checks below).

Through the public `graph.execute()` path on the same GPU (with `CUDNN_FRONTEND_ENABLE_FROST_ENGINES=1`, since the FROST GEMM engine
is opt-in), the first cuDNN backend plan (engine 10) for `y = cmp_op(C, X)` returns IEEE masks, and the FROST plan (engine 20400) did
not on develop. So the two engines gave the same graph different results,
while Rule 9 of `python/cudnn/AGENTS.md` asks backend and FROST to keep the same semantics for a graph both support. With this
change they agree (counts under Testing).

A native compare has IEEE semantics by construction: the ordered predicates are false when an operand is NaN, the unordered `UNE` is
true, and equal infinities compare equal. No arithmetic on `a - b` can give `cmp_eq` / `cmp_le` / `cmp_ge` for equal infinities, so
patching the NaN handling of `max` / `min` would not be enough. `vector.where` over a vector compare is the lowering `binary_select`
and the mainloop K-tail mask already use in this module, so this adds no new CuTe DSL dependency.

The change is outside `python/cudnn/gemm/frost/sm120/` because, since #1993, the emitter lives only in the shared
`python/cudnn/gemm/frost/epilogue_codegen.py`, whose `_emit_pointwise_dag` both arch families call
(`sm120/epilogue_codegen.py:827`, `sm100/epilogue_codegen.py:498`). There is no per-family copy to fix instead.

Found in an audit of the SM120 Frost kernel templates (finding B09).

## Related issues

None.

Related PRs from the same audit that change `python/cudnn/gemm/frost/epilogue_codegen.py`:

- #2022 (G4.4, int32-compute epilogue ops) makes SM120 decline int32-compute `cmp_*` ops (in `sm120/compiler.py`). Those are the only
  graphs that still reach the step form left in the `cmp_*` branch of `_emit_binary_ext`; SM100 has no such check (see "API and
  compatibility impact").
- #2030 (G4.1, `mod`), #2026 (G4.3, default `relu_backward`) and #2009 (B10, `relu` / `relu_backward` with a slope) change other
  branches of `_emit_binary_ext`; G4.1 and G4.3 also replace step forms there.
- #2012 (G4.2), #2025 (B11), #2014 (B13) and #2013 (B14) change other emitters in the same file.

`git merge-tree` merges each of these branches with this one without conflicts.

## API and compatibility impact

- No API change.
- Numerics: under fp32 compute, `cmp_*` masks change only where an operand is NaN or both operands are the same infinity; they now
  match IEEE comparison and torch, and in the `graph.execute()` check under Testing they match cuDNN backend engine 10 on the same
  graphs. Masks for finite operands are unchanged.
- SM100: the emitter is shared, so the SM100 tree (dense, block-scale, MoE, the split-K reduction epilogue and SM100 mainloop-fusion
  transforms) gets the same fix. It was not run on SM100 hardware here; the existing SM100 cmp cases in
  `test_matmul_epilogue_fusion.py::test_pointwise_mode_coverage` (finite inputs) exercise the new code on SM100 CI.
- INT32 compute is unchanged: a `cmp_*` node with `compute_data_type=INT32` still takes the step form and still fails at build with
  `TypeError: floor is only supported for floating-point types`. That failure is a separate audit finding (G4.4); its PR #2022
  declines such graphs on SM120. `sm100/compiler.py` has no such check, so removing the int32 step form is left for a follow-up.
- Chains with `cmp_*` ops render different kernel source, so their cached kernels are rebuilt once.

## Testing

frontend bindings built from develop 24a8cd43. All commands from `test/python`.

+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright (c) 2026 NVIDIA CORPORATION & AFFILIATES. All rights reserved.
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+
+"""cmp_* epilogue ops keep IEEE comparison semantics for non-finite operands.
+
+The stored 0/1 masks must equal torch's comparisons cell for cell: a NaN operand
+compares false (true for cmp_neq), equal infinities compare equal, and finite
+operands, subnormals included, stay exact. Covers an aux operand on either side
+of the compare, two chain operands (the isnan idiom cmp_neq(C, C)) and a scalar
+operand (the isfinite idiom cmp_lt(abs(C), inf))."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+import cudnn
+import cudnn.gemm.frost  # noqa: F401  — installs the cudnn.pygraph recorder hook
+from cudnn.gemm.frost.tile_config import by_name
+
+from gemm_test_utils import Plan as _plan, requires_sm120
+
+pytestmark = [pytest.mark.L0, requires_sm120]
+
+_M = _N = _K = 128
+_INF, _NAN = float("inf"), float("nan")
+_SUBNORMAL = 1.401298464324817e-45  # smallest positive fp32 subnormal
+_CMP_OPS = {"cmp_eq": torch.eq, "cmp_neq": torch.ne, "cmp_lt": torch.lt, "cmp_le": torch.le, "cmp_gt": torch.gt, "cmp_ge": torch.ge}
+
+# Row bands of C, and what the aux X holds there (even / odd columns).
+_BANDS = {
+    "C=+inf, X=+inf/3e38": (0, 16),
+    "C=-inf, X=-inf/-3e38": (16, 32),
+    "C=NaN, X=0": (32, 48),
+    "C finite, X=NaN": (48, 64),
+    "C finite, X=-inf/+inf": (64, 80),
+    "C finite, X=C/C+-d": (80, 112),
+    "C=0, X=-sub/+sub": (112, 128),
+}
+
+
+def _operands():
+    """A, B (as [N, K]), the exact fp32 accumulator C = A @ B and the aux X."""
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    a = torch.randint(-2, 3, (_M, _K)).float()
+    b = torch.randint(-2, 3, (_N, _K)).float()
+    b[:, 0] = 1.0  # a non-finite A[r, 0] then fills row r of C with that value
+    a[112:] = 0.0
+    acc = (a.double() @ b.double().T).float()  # exact: small integers
+    for (r0, r1), v in (((0, 16), _INF), ((16, 32), -_INF), ((32, 48), _NAN)):
+        a[r0:r1, 0] = v
+        acc[r0:r1] = v
+    odd = torch.arange(_N) % 2 == 1
+    x = acc.clone()
+    x[0:16] = torch.where(odd, 3e38, _INF)
+    x[16:32] = torch.where(odd, -3e38, -_INF)
+    x[32:48] = 0.0
+    x[48:64] = _NAN
+    x[64:80] = torch.where(odd, _INF, -_INF)
+    x[80:112] += torch.tensor([0.0, 0.5, 0.0, -0.5, 0.0, 1.0, 0.0, -1.0]).repeat(_N // 8)
+    x[112:128] = torch.where(odd, _SUBNORMAL, -_SUBNORMAL)
+    return a, b, acc, x
+
+
+def test_cmp_ops_follow_ieee_for_nonfinite_operands_sm120():
+    """The six cmp ops with the aux on either side, the isnan idiom and the isfinite
+    idiom on +-inf, NaN and subnormal operands, dense sm120 matmul with an fp32 epilogue."""
+    g = cudnn.pygraph(io_data_type=cudnn.data_type.BFLOAT16, intermediate_data_type=cudnn.data_type.FLOAT, compute_data_type=cudnn.data_type.FLOAT)
+    A = g.tensor(name="A", dim=[1, _M, _K], stride=[_M * _K, _K, 1])
+    B = g.tensor(name="B", dim=[1, _K, _N], stride=[_K * _N, 1, _K])
+    C = g.matmul(A=A, B=B, name="mm")
+    X = g.tensor(name="x", dim=[1, _M, _N], stride=[_M * _N, _N, 1], data_type=cudnn.data_type.FLOAT)
+    inf = g.tensor(name="inf", dim=[1, 1, 1], stride=[1, 1, 1], data_type=cudnn.data_type.FLOAT)
+    ys = {op: getattr(g, op)(input=C, comparison=X, name=f"y_{op}") for op in _CMP_OPS}
+    ys.update({f"{op}(X, C)": getattr(g, op)(input=X, comparison=C, name=f"y_{op}_xc") for op in _CMP_OPS})  # aux on the left
+    ys["isnan"] = g.cmp_neq(input=C, comparison=C, name="y_isnan")
+    ys["isfinite"] = g.cmp_lt(input=g.abs(input=C, name="abs"), comparison=inf, name="y_isfinite")
+    for y in ys.values():
+        y.set_data_type(cudnn.data_type.FLOAT).set_output(True)
+    compiled = _plan(g, config=by_name("CONFIG_sm120_128x128x128_16x16x32_cluster1x1_warps4x2"))
+
+    a, b, acc, x = _operands()
+    outs = {name: torch.full((1, _M, _N), _NAN, device="cuda") for name in ys}
+    variant_pack = {
+        A: a.to(torch.bfloat16).view(1, _M, _K).cuda(),
+        B: b.to(torch.bfloat16).view(1, _N, _K).transpose(1, 2).cuda(),
+        X: x.view(1, _M, _N).cuda(),
+        inf: torch.full((1, 1, 1), _INF, device="cuda"),
+    }
+    variant_pack.update({ys[name]: out for name, out in outs.items()})
+    compiled(variant_pack)
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+
+    refs = {op: fn(acc, x) for op, fn in _CMP_OPS.items()}
+    refs.update({f"{op}(X, C)": fn(x, acc) for op, fn in _CMP_OPS.items()})
+    refs["isnan"] = torch.isnan(acc)
+    refs["isfinite"] = torch.isfinite(acc)
+    bad = {}
+    for name, ref in refs.items():
+        got = outs[name][0].cpu()
+        for band, (r0, r1) in _BANDS.items():
+            n = int((got[r0:r1] != ref[r0:r1].float()).sum())
+            if n:
+                bad[f"{name} @ {band}"] = n
+    assert not bad, f"cmp masks differ from IEEE comparisons (mismatching cells of {_N} per row): {bad}"

**Codex bot review · model: `gpt-6-astra`**

Reviewed `3aa6001c5c01` against base `0f5c79988df0`.

No actionable defect found. Native FP32 comparisons fix equal-infinity and NaN masks while preserving the tested finite and subnormal cases. The shared change works through both compiler families on native SM100, including equality/inequality mainloop transforms on both operands. The existing INT32 comparison path is unchanged.

Validation: Reviewed both changed files and traced the shared vector emitter through epilogue and mainloop generation. Ordered comparisons and unordered not-equal produce the expected numeric 0/1 masks. The new regression passed through each compiler family on native SM100: eight masks with 16,384 cells each, including all six comparisons plus isnan/isfinite idioms. The CPU reference covers NaNs on either side, equal infinities, finite differences and the smallest FP32 subnormals. Restoring the base emitter reproduced the equal-infinity failures for all six comparisons and NaN failures for strict less/greater comparisons on the same SM100 route. The change combines cleanly with the current base. Four independent mainloop plans on that combined source passed 24 CUDA graph replays: equality/inequality on A and B, K=136, changing scalar comparisons against zero, infinity and NaN. Outputs matched independent CPU masks exactly, with paired bit-identical replays after output poisoning. Requested python/gemm/frost CI for the current head. Existing SM100 comparison cases run in that lane; the new SM120-marked regression will skip.

Limitations: No native SM120, MoE or block-scale comparison execution, and no performance measurement. Repeatability evidence covers the tested configurations; INT32 behavior was not changed or newly qualified.

Approved: no P0 or high-risk P1 found. Remaining findings stay with the owner; merge timing stays with the owner.
